title: The hold, its reason and its review date have no durable home, no state name and no requirement row
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.1, T3.3); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.10.2, A2.10.3.2, T8); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-010 Data table); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (Sheet: States, Sheet: Route sets)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3 and 8; s8 BR1, BR2, BR10; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13 Database and migrations; CON s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned
description: The feature holds a case with a reason and a date the hold is reviewed, and nothing in the read sources says where that hold is persisted. The ownership rows of the context pack give S1 no table at all, so the service schema can hold only the library objects of DP-03 and the idempotency key. The legacy Data table of RWB-E4-010 names recovery_case, assignment, decision_log_entry and rule_row, which belong to P3 and P7 and carry no hold or review-date field. TSD S1 T3.1 declares only valuation and score, and neither carries a hold. The States sheet of the routing logic covers the ten route sets and has no route-decision set, so no held state is named for the route decision, and the requirement table of FSD S1 T8 maps REQ-S1-001 to REQ-S1-008 to the appraisal, the return by route, the payoff, the recommendation, the approval and a fresh decision on a change, and carries no requirement row for a hold. The stories therefore record the hold, its reason and its review date in the local decision record, answer the case move and the task to rwb-case, and leave the durable column and the state name open instead of inventing them.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack list no table under S1; the legacy Data table of RWB-E4-010 lists recovery_case (DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023), assignment (DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016), decision_log_entry (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018) and rule_row (DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015) and no hold field; TSD S1 T3.1 declares valuation (DF-COL-018 to DF-COL-027, DF-COL-043, DF-COL-044) and score (DF-DEC-019 to DF-DEC-027); the FSD S1 A2.10.3.2 field catalog lists v_ace_valuation and valuation_ext fields only; the routing logic States sheet has 228 states across the ten route sets and none of them is a route-decision hold; FSD S1 T8 lists REQ-S1-001 to REQ-S1-008 and none names a hold or a review date.
area: Data model and case state, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P3 rwb-case owner and the data steward
proposed: Carry the hold, its reason and its review date in the local decision record and on the case of record, declare no column and no state name in rwb_valuation, and let the data owner and the P3 owner name a column and a held state later in a minor contract version.

title: The review date has no clock owner, no rule row and no Schedule, and the prerequisite FEAT-CWC-11 has no published identity
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1: no job, one workflow RouteDecisionWorkflow); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.10.2, A2.10.4.4); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-VAL-10 depends on FEAT-CWC-11); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (Sheet: Rules, Sheet: Events); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-10, R5.7)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s8 BR3, BR10; s9 State transitions; s12.6 Schedules; s13 Build steps 7 and 8; CON s3, s6, s12.5, s12.6
description: The hold exists to bring a case back on a date the owner sets, and no source says which component owns that clock. The ownership rows give S1 no job, so no Quartz job of the module survives the split and no Temporal Schedule can be declared for the service. FSD S1 A2.10.4.4 declares no background event for the feature. The routing logic publishes the event code REVIEW_DATE_REACHED but consumes it only in the litigation set (R-LIT-55, R-LIT-56) and the write-off set (R-WO-17, R-WO-19); no rule row of the route decision fires a review date, and the route decision has no rule set of its own in the Rules sheet. The prerequisite the features sheet names, FEAT-CWC-11, carries no name, no owner and no contract row in the read sources. The stories therefore wait on a durable timer of RouteDecisionWorkflow on rwb-valuation, declare no Schedule and no job, answer the lift and the task to rwb-case, and record the ownership of the clock as open.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack list no job under S1 and one workflow, RouteDecisionWorkflow; FSD S1 A2.10.4.4 is the row None, No background event; the routing logic Rules sheet has REVIEW_DATE_REACHED only in R-LIT-55, R-LIT-56, R-WO-17 and R-WO-19; the Events sheet lists REVIEW_DATE_REACHED with two consuming route sets, Litigation and Write-off; the features sheet of the Epics 3 to 8 specification names FEAT-CWC-11 as the only dependency of FEAT-VAL-10 and no document in the read list defines that feature.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P3 rwb-case owner
proposed: Wait on a durable timer of RouteDecisionWorkflow on the rwb-valuation task queue, declare no Schedule and no Quartz job, and take the lift move and the task answer from rwb-case; the P3 owner confirms the held state and the clock when FEAT-CWC-11 is published.

title: The field catalog of FEAT-VAL-10 carries the valuation fields and publishes no hold field, no reason code and no bound on the review date
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.10.3.1, A2.10.3.2, A2.4.3.2); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-VAL-10, FEAT-VAL-04); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-010 Validation and messages); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.2)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 4; s5 X6; s7; s8 BR4; s11 Data; s13 Configuration and reference data; CON s3, s8 BR7, s12.2
description: The hold needs a reason and a date, and neither has a published shape. The field catalog of FSD S1 A2.10.3.2 is the catalog of A2.4 and lists the v_ace_valuation appraisals and the valuation_ext valuer: it carries no hold reason, no review date and no hold flag, so the feature's field list is a copy of the acceptance feature and not a list of the hold. No source publishes a list of hold reason codes, an LOV for them, or a bound on the review date: no minimum interval, no maximum hold and no hold limit appears in the FSD, the TSD, the features sheet or the routing logic, and TSD S1 T3.2 gives only LOV-APPRAISAL and LOV-ROUTE. BR-S1-010 forbids writing a value a business person may change in code, so the stories read the reason as a code of the business date, refuse a code that is not in the list, record the review date as given and assert no bound; the conflict in the catalog is recorded as a gap for the data owner.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.10.3.2 lists v_ace_valuation.valuation_key, asset_key, appraisal_no, appraisal_type, appraised_value, forced_sale_value, appraisal_date and valuation_ext.valuer_partner_id, and no hold field; the same table is the field catalog of A2.4; the legacy message set of RWB-E4-010 carries MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 and no message for a reason code or a date; TSD S1 T3.2 gives LOV-APPRAISAL and LOV-ROUTE only; no row of the routing logic mentions a hold limit for the route decision or a reason code list.
area: Data dictionary and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the data steward and the reference-data owner
proposed: Record the reason as a coded value of reference data read with its version, refuse a code that is not in the list of the business date with MSG-GEN-001, record the review date as given with no bound, and keep the catalog entry for the hold open until the data owner publishes it.

title: The element set of RouteRequest and Approval and the names of the four consumed rows are not published, and the plan carries no C row
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2 API-S1-001, T5.1, T5.2); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-010 Endpoints table); _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP table, R5.7)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s7 C2; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13; APP s3, s12.1, s12.2, s12.8
description: TSD S1 T-A.2 names the request type RouteRequest and the response type Approval and publishes no field table for either, the legacy story names the operation and no body, and the Ownership Map names no operation that writes a hold of its own. The hold therefore cannot be declared as a required element of a route submission without a default. The same holds for the four rows the step consumes: the case-state read and the hold-move answer of rwb-case, the rule-in-force, reason-code and decision-log read of rwb-decision and the authorise operation of rwb-access, where only the access row has a published name. TSD S1 T5.1 is the row None and T5.2 lists the calls to P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 without an operation. The DP table adds no C dependency for DP-03, DP-13 and DP-19, so the plan's contract row for both stories is empty and both build and test against the documented use, the placeholder and the fakes from Day 1.
evidence: TSD S1 T-A.2 gives Purpose, Request RouteRequest, Response Approval, Errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, Authorization and Idempotency, and no field list; the legacy Endpoints table of RWB-E4-010 gives one row, POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/route, with access Treatment and offer U; the ownership rows of the context pack give three S1 operations and none of them is a hold write; TSD S1 T5.1 is None and T5.2 names P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 without an operation; the plan rows for RWB-S1-E4010-APP and -CON carry C as an empty list.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P3, P7 and P4 owners
proposed: Declare the hold reason and the review date as optional elements of the one published route operation and declare no second operation; build the four consumed rows against their documented use, a placeholder operation name and a fake, and replace the placeholder in a minor contract version when an owner publishes a name.
